title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page belongs to a long hand computation in the 'Action de Galois sur Teichmüller' notes. Grothendieck is determining the automorphisms of a profinite fundamental groupoid (called 'VI_3' here). Its vertex group is \hat Π_{0,3}, the profinite fundamental group of P^1−{0,1,∞}, free profinite on two generators. The groupoid carries the S_3-type symmetries of {0,1,∞}: ρ, apparently the order-3 rotation; σ_∞ and σ_0, apparently involutions; and ε_0, a further automorphism of \hat Π_{0,3}. An automorphism u that fixes the vertices is encoded by parameters λ, η, ξ ∈ \hat Π_{0,3}. These parameters give the action of u on the chosen paths b_i^ω, \tilde b_i^ω, \tilde a_i^ω through the auxiliary quantities β, α, \tilde α of (57). The conditions u must satisfy are (55). Eliminating \tilde α gave the single relation (56): η^{-1}ε_0(λη) = ξ ρ^{-1}(ξ)^{-1}. Page 16 introduced the inverted quantities β' = β^{-1} = η σ_∞(η)^{-1} and α' = α^{-1}, with β' = α' σ_∞(λ) (equation (59)).

This page rewrites (56) in a 'more congenial' coboundary form, (60): α' = ξ' ρ^{±1}(ξ')^{-1}, i.e. η σ_∞(η)^{-1} = (ξ' ρ(ξ')^{-1}) σ_∞(λ).

Proof given:
- The earlier formula α = ρ(η \tilde α ρ^{-1}(η)^{-1}), quoted as '(75bis)', is inverted. With \tilde α' := \tilde α^{-1} this gives α' = ρ(ρ^{-1}(η) \tilde α' η^{-1}) = η ρ(\tilde α') ρ(η)^{-1}, which is (61).
- The second relation of (55), \tilde α = ξ ρ^{-1}(ξ)^{-1}, inverts to \tilde α' = ρ^{-1}(ξ) ξ^{-1}. Hence ρ(\tilde α') = ξ ρ(ξ)^{-1}.
- Substituting: α' = η ξ ρ(ξ)^{-1} ρ(η)^{-1} = (ηξ) ρ(ηξ)^{-1}. This is (60) with ξ' = ηξ.

Summary (62): the vertex-fixing automorphisms of the groupoid VI_3 that correspond to the action of 𝔊_3 are parametrized by triples (λ, η, ξ') ∈ \hat Π_{0,3}^3 satisfying the relation, which he calls 'relation des tresses/lacets ?' with a question mark. Explicitly: η σ_∞(η)^{-1} = ξ' ρ(ξ')^{-1} σ_∞(λ). Equivalently, writing β' = η σ_∞(η)^{-1} and α' = ξ' ρ(ξ')^{-1}, the condition is β' = α' σ_∞(λ). The next page restates this as (63) and reinterprets α', β', ξ' geometrically via inverted paths.

Purpose: this is a step toward describing the automorphism group of the genus-0 'Teichmüller' groupoid at low level. Each automorphism is given by a 'twist' parameter λ (later specialised to a power ℓ_0^γ of a loop) together with cocycle/coboundary-type data relative to the symmetries σ_∞ and ρ. These are the 2-cycle/3-cycle (involution/rotation) relations familiar from the later Grothendieck–Teichmüller group.
errors: Sign/exponent inconsistency. The derivation on the page yields α' = ξ' ρ(ξ')^{-1}, with ρ and not ρ^{-1}; the second line of (60) also uses ρ. The first line of (60), as transcribed and as repeated in (63) on the next page, has ρ^{-1}(ξ')^{-1}. In the image the exponent in (60) looks overwritten, so this is either a slip or a convention change. The computed version (ρ) is the one justified on the page.

The cross-reference '(75bis)' does not fit the local numbering, where equations here run 55–62. It is probably a slip for an earlier formula, likely the first relation of (55)/(57), or a reference to another batch of notes.

Equivalence (56) ⇔ (60) is fine given the change of variable ξ' = ηξ, which is a bijection for fixed η. The summary (62) is presented as a parametrization 'satisfying the relation …?'. The question mark suggests he had not yet checked whether further (braid-type) relations are required, so completeness of the parametrization is not established on this page.

ideas.what: Parametrizing vertex-fixing automorphisms of a profinite fundamental groupoid of P^1−{0,1,∞}/M_{0,4} by elements of \hat F_2 satisfying twisted-coboundary relations relative to the S_3 symmetries (involution σ_∞, rotation ρ)
ideas.modern_name: Precursor of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group \hat{GT} (pairs (λ,f) with 2-cycle and 3-cycle/hexagon relations)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1991); program sketched by Grothendieck in Esquisse d'un programme (1984)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) states the program (Teichmüller tower, Galois action, relations at levels 1 and 2) but does not contain such explicit formulas

ideas.what: Rewriting the cocycle condition as a ρ-coboundary condition α' = ξ'ρ(ξ')^{-1} after the substitution ξ' = ηξ
ideas.modern_name: Coboundary/normalisation of nonabelian 1-cocycles for a finite group of outer automorphisms

ideas.what: Inverting paths (b' = b^{-1}, etc.) to turn right-twisted formulas into left-twisted ones
ideas.modern_name: Groupoid inversion / change of path orientation conventions

missed.claim: Grothendieck obtains an explicit three-parameter description (λ, η, ξ') ∈ \hat Π_{0,3}^3 of the automorphisms of his level-3 genus-0 groupoid, constrained by an involution relation and a rotation relation. He leaves open (question mark) whether a further braid/loop relation is needed. This is an independent, pre-Drinfeld route toward \hat{GT}-type relations, in a coboundary form rather than Drinfeld's f(x,y) form. Comparing his parametrization with the standard (λ,f) one, and seeing whether his extra parameters η, ξ' correspond to known 'semi-GT'-style data, is a historically interesting but specialised question.
missed.quote: En résumé les automorph. du groupoïde VI_3, induisant l'identité sur les sommets et correspondant à l'action de 𝔊_3 correspondent aux (λ,η,ξ') ∈ Π̂_{0,3}×Π̂_{0,3}×Π̂_{0,3} satisfaisant la relation des tresses ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's own explicit computations toward \hat{GT} before Drinfeld/Ihara. It may give an alternative coboundary presentation of the 2- and 3-cycle relations, of interest to historians and to people studying variants of GT (e.g. Schneps, Lochak, Nakamura). The content itself is likely recoverable from the known theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine algebraic manipulation (inverting and substituting) inside a larger computation. Its interest is historical: it shows Grothendieck explicitly parametrizing automorphisms of a genus-0 profinite groupoid by \hat F_2-data with involution/rotation relations, a GT precursor. Specialists already know, at least in outline, that such computations exist in these archives, and no new result beyond known GT theory is visible here.
